Translate English to First-Order Logic.

Compiles a natural-language sentence to formal logic — the LOGOS logic mode from the terminal. Reads the sentence inline, from `--file`, or from piped stdin. Prints bare FOL on stdout, so output pipes cleanly into other tools.

Usage: largo logic [OPTIONS] [SENTENCE]

Arguments:
  [SENTENCE]
          The English sentence to translate

Options:
  -f, --file <FILE>
          Read the sentence (or discourse) from a file

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format for the logical form

          Possible values:
          - unicode: Unicode logic symbols: ∀, ∃, ∧, ∨, ¬, →
          - latex:   LaTeX markup: \forall, \exists, \land, ...
          - ascii:   Plain ASCII FOL
          - kripke:  Kripke semantics: modals lowered to explicit world quantification
          
          [default: unicode]

      --all-readings
          Show every reading (quantifier scopes + parse forest), numbered

      --pragmatic
          Enrich with scalar implicature (pragmatic strengthening)

      --discourse
          Treat each input line as one sentence of a discourse with shared anaphora context

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress informational output (errors still print)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase output verbosity (repeatable)

      --color <WHEN>
          When to use terminal colors

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Color when stdout/stderr is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even into pipes (CI logs, `less -R`)
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  largo logic "Every woman loves a man."
  largo logic "Every woman loves a man." --all-readings
  largo logic "It might rain." --format kripke
  echo "Socrates is mortal." | largo logic
  printf 'A farmer owns a donkey.\nHe feeds it.' | largo logic --discourse
